briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Repeal Momentum Builds in Michigan as DEA Opens Schedule III Door and Compass Pathways Nears the Finish Line
briefs.top: Michigan operators are getting real signals of relief — a fresh repeal bill, steady consumer demand, and a gubernatorial candidate campaigning against the 24% wholesale tax — even as a wetlands ruling reminds growers compliance still matters. Nationally, the DEA just opened a concrete Schedule III pathway for medical cannabis firms, Curaleaf is sweetening its Aurora takeover, and Compass Pathways planted a flag in Jersey City as its psilocybin NDA races toward Q4.

local.text: Lawmakers float new bill to kill the tax — Michigan's cannabis market is feeling the weight of the 24% wholesale tax, with dispensary closures climbing and a fresh repeal bill now on the table in Lansing.

Muskegon bets big on a new retail format — operators are pushing into hospitality-forward territory, with a dispensary-restaurant buildout in Muskegon that pushes the format further than most Michigan stores have gone.

Consumer demand isn't cracking under the tax — despite the new 24% levy, that drop-to-black-market scenario doesn't seem to be the case so far in 2026 for Michiganders, with licensed businesses absorbing costs in an oversupplied market rather than passing them on.

A governor's race contender takes aim at the tax — Genesee County Sheriff Chris Swanson, a Democratic gubernatorial primary candidate, called the new tax "not fair and equitable" and promised to work to repeal it.

Court flags a wetlands compliance failure — a Michigan marijuana cultivator illegally destroyed 15.9 acres of protected wetlands to build a cannabis farm, a state court determined this week, a cautionary tale for operators on land-use diligence.

national.text: DEA opens a real Schedule III on-ramp — state-licensed medical cannabis businesses can now use the new Form 225 application process to register under the Controlled Substances Act after the initial 60-day expedited window closed.

Curaleaf raises the stakes on Aurora — the company increased its total implied consideration by 25% to US$5 per Aurora share, a premium of 86% to Aurora's unaffected share price, in its bid to build a global cannabis giant.

Compass Pathways plants its US flag — the UK-based psilocybin company opened its U.S. office in Jersey City this week, with its COMP360 NDA still expected to be complete in Q4 2026 and a commercial launch targeted for the first half of 2027.

Rescheduling hits a pause, not a dead end — the latest development is a procedural pause, not a rejection, after a DEA judge stayed the Schedule III proceeding over a new GAO report, with the government's response due October 13.

Spherex expands its Colorado footprint — the company is acquiring two cultivation facilities in Colorado from The Cannabist Company and its affiliates, the latest consolidation move in a fast-moving MSO landscape.
